The user is still seeing the input bar “snap” away from the bottom of the screen while the agent is running. In the previous fix I promised to pin the input bar permanently at the bottom and to queue any typed messages that arrive while the agent is busy. 

To make that work, the Input component must stay mounted at all times, but it should ignore key events when the UI is in a state where the input shouldn’t be interactive (for example, while the agent is processing a command or when a modal has focus). The existing `InputProps` interface only includes callbacks and a `suggestionsCount` flag; there’s no way for the parent layout to tell the input to temporarily become inert. 

The cleanest solution is to add an `active` boolean prop that defaults to `true`. When `active` is `false`, the component will still render (so the layout stays stable) but will ignore key presses. This will prevent the “unmount‑while‑running” behavior that causes the snapping. I don’t need to change any other files right now—just expose the prop and give it a default value in the function parameters.

Then I’ll modify the function signature to destructure `active = true` from the props, ensuring the default is true so existing usage isn’t broken. I’ll keep the rest of the file unchanged. The edit should be a non‑global replace (replace_all: false) targeting just the old snippet and swapping it for the new one that includes the `active` prop.
